baseTier.label: Severe hypertension (no organ-damage features)
baseTier.action: Confirm with a repeat reading after rest; do NOT lower acutely if asymptomatic (risk of harm); optimise oral therapy + arrange timely follow-up; screen for target-organ damage.

anyOf.feature: severe headache, visual disturbance, confusion or seizures (encephalopathy)
tearing chest/back pain / unequal pulses (aortic dissection)
pregnancy >20wks with headache / visual symptoms / RUQ pain (pre-eclampsia/eclampsia)
reduced urine output / acute kidney injury

tier.label: Hypertensive emergency (acute hypertension-mediated target-organ damage)
ddx: acute coronary syndrome / acute LV failure / pulmonary oedema
tier.action: EMERGENCY: controlled IV BP reduction, syndrome-specific (NOT aggressive lowering in acute ischaemic stroke; rapid control in dissection / eclampsia / pulmonary oedema); urgent ECG, U&E/creatinine, urinalysis, fundoscopy, imaging as indicated; admit (ICU/HDU). Clinician-led.

citation: ESC 2024 / AHA 2024 / ACC-AHA 2017 — CSO to set the diastolic emergency cut (ESC >=110 vs AHA >=120) + align with the Uganda Clinical Guidelines. In pregnancy use MEOWS + MgSO4 for eclampsia.

baseTier.label: Hypotension (isolated low systolic BP)
baseTier.action: Confirm reading + posture; assess perfusion (pulse, capillary refill, mentation, urine output); find the cause; fluid as indicated by volume status. Trend matters more than a single value.

anyOf.feature: tachycardia + cool peripheries / prolonged capillary refill / mottling

tier.label: Shock / haemodynamic compromise
ddx: hypovolaemic shock (haemorrhage, GI loss, severe dehydration)
obstructive shock (tension pneumothorax, tamponade, massive PE)
tier.action: EMERGENCY: ABCDE, high-flow oxygen, large-bore IV access, restore circulation per cause; if sepsis — cultures + early antibiotics + measured resuscitation; treat the specific shock type (adrenaline for anaphylaxis, decompress tension pneumothorax, control haemorrhage); senior help; admit ICU/HDU.

citation: Sepsis-3 / qSOFA 2016; Surviving Sepsis Campaign; RCP NEWS2 2017; WHO/FEAST 2011 — CSO to set the flag band (<=90 NEWS2-red vs <=100 qSOFA) + confirm the FEAST guardrail (no fluid boluses in febrile non-hypotensive children).

baseTier.label: Hypoxaemia (low oxygen saturation)
baseTier.action: Confirm a good trace; controlled oxygen to target (88-92% if hypercapnic risk, else 94-98%); identify + treat the cause; reassess RR + work of breathing together (SpO2 alone underestimates distress). In severe anaemia SpO2 can read normal despite low O2 content.

anyOf.feature: unable to speak full sentences / exhaustion / silent chest
altered mental status / agitation or drowsiness (CO2 retention)

tier.label: Acute respiratory failure / impending arrest
tier.action: EMERGENCY: ABCDE, high-flow / titrated oxygen, treat the cause urgently (bronchodilators, decompress tension pneumothorax); consider ventilatory support (NIV / intubation); senior + critical-care help; admit.

citation: RCP NEWS2 2017; BTS oxygen 2017 — CSO to define Scale 1 vs Scale 2 selection (COPD / hypercapnic risk) + any altitude/locale baseline adjustment.

baseTier.label: Tachypnoea (raised respiratory rate)
baseTier.action: RR is the most sensitive early-deterioration sign — count for a full minute. Identify + treat the cause; reassess with SpO2 + work of breathing. A rising RR warns even when other vitals are normal.

tier.label: Respiratory failure / peri-arrest
tier.action: EMERGENCY: ABCDE; oxygen; treat the cause (bronchodilators; fluids + insulin for DKA per protocol); ventilatory support if needed; senior / critical-care help; admit.

baseTier.label: Bradypnoea (low respiratory rate)
baseTier.action: Count for a full minute; consider opioid / sedative effect (reverse if indicated), CNS pathology and pre-arrest fatigue; support ventilation if hypoventilating.

tier.label: Hypoventilation / impending arrest
tier.action: EMERGENCY: ABCDE; support ventilation; naloxone for opioid toxicity; senior / critical-care help; admit.

baseTier.label: Bradycardia
baseTier.action: 12-lead ECG; review medications + electrolytes; assess symptoms / perfusion; treat reversible causes (e.g. hyperkalaemia, drug toxicity).

tier.label: Adverse / unstable bradycardia
ddx: complete (3rd-degree) or Mobitz II AV block
tier.action: EMERGENCY per the Resuscitation Council adult bradycardia algorithm: atropine; if refractory, transcutaneous pacing / chronotropic infusion; treat toxic / electrolyte cause; senior + cardiology; continuous monitoring.

citation: RCP NEWS2 2017; Resuscitation Council adult bradycardia algorithm. Pacing often unavailable — stabilise medically (atropine, treat hyperkalaemia) + refer.

baseTier.label: Tachycardia
baseTier.action: 12-lead ECG to define the rhythm; identify + treat the cause (often compensatory — find what it is compensating for); reassess BP + perfusion. Treat the cause, not the number.

tier.label: Unstable tachyarrhythmia / decompensation
ddx: septic or hypovolaemic shock with compensatory tachycardia
tier.action: EMERGENCY: ABCDE; a tachyarrhythmia with adverse features — synchronised DC cardioversion per the Resuscitation Council algorithm; if compensatory — treat the underlying shock / sepsis / haemorrhage; senior help; monitoring; admit.

citation: RCP NEWS2 2017; Resuscitation Council adult tachycardia algorithm. Distinguish a compensatory sinus tachycardia from a primary arrhythmia.

baseTier.label: Fever / pyrexia
baseTier.action: Find the source (history, exam, focused tests); in an endemic area TEST FOR MALARIA (RDT/film) in any fever; antipyretics for comfort; reassess for sepsis features. Fever is a symptom — the priority is the cause.

anyOf.feature: signs of shock (low BP, poor perfusion)

tier.label: Sepsis / serious infection (e.g. meningitis, severe malaria)
tier.action: EMERGENCY: treat as sepsis — cultures + EARLY broad-spectrum antibiotics, measured fluid resuscitation, oxygen, source control; if meningitis suspected don't delay antibiotics; if malaria — IV artesunate; senior help; admit. Treat on clinical suspicion.

citation: Surviving Sepsis Campaign; Sepsis-3 / qSOFA 2016; WHO malaria 2025; UCG. Exclude malaria in EVERY fever; FEAST: no fluid boluses in febrile non-hypotensive children.

baseTier.label: Hypothermia (<=35.0 C)
ddx: sepsis (hypothermia is a sepsis sign, esp. elderly / immunocompromised)
baseTier.action: Confirm with a low-reading (core) thermometer; rewarm; CRUCIALLY find the cause — hypothermia in an unwell adult often signals sepsis, not just cold. Check capillary glucose.

tier.label: Hypothermic sepsis / myxoedema coma / decompensation
tier.action: EMERGENCY: ABCDE; active rewarming; treat sepsis (cultures + early antibiotics + resuscitation) if infection suspected; correct glucose; if myxoedema coma — thyroid hormone + steroids per protocol; cardiac monitoring (arrhythmia risk); senior help; admit.

citation: RCP NEWS2 2017; Surviving Sepsis Campaign. Always check capillary glucose.

baseTier.label: Hypoglycaemia (3.0-3.8 mmol/L)
baseTier.action: Treat now: 15-20 g fast-acting oral carbohydrate if conscious + able to swallow; recheck in ~15 min and repeat until >=4.0 mmol/L; then a longer-acting carbohydrate; review insulin / sulfonylurea. Always check glucose in any unwell or altered patient ('Don't Ever Forget Glucose').

anyOf.feature: unable to swallow / reduced consciousness / coma

tier.label: Severe hypoglycaemia — neuroglycopenic emergency
tier.action: EMERGENCY: if IV access — IV glucose per protocol; if not — IM glucagon; recheck + repeat; protect the airway; sulfonylurea / recurrent → admit (consider octreotide); treat the cause; recheck after recovery (relapse is common). Doses via the prescribing engine.

citation: ADA Standards of Care 2024-2026 — CSO to confirm the point-of-care assay + units (mmol/L vs mg/dL). Treatment doses live in the prescribing engine, not here.

baseTier.label: Marked hyperglycaemia
baseTier.action: Confirm; CHECK KETONES (blood beta-hydroxybutyrate ideally, or urine) + hydration; assess for an intercurrent illness / infection; review / adjust therapy. Ketones + symptoms → the DKA/HHS pathway.

tier.label: Hyperglycaemic emergency (DKA or HHS)
tier.action: EMERGENCY: confirm with ketones / venous gas / U&E; manage per the current DKA/HHS consensus — IV fluids, fixed-rate IV insulin (or SC for mild uncomplicated DKA where appropriate), potassium replacement, treat the precipitant, monitor closely; senior help; admit. Doses/rates via protocol + the prescribing engine.

citation: Hyperglycaemic crises consensus 2024; ADA 2024-2026; UCG — CSO to set the flag band (>11 vs >14 mmol/L, assay/unit dependent) + confirm the DKA/HHS criteria. Doses live in the prescribing engine.

baseTier.label: GCS <=8 — airway at risk
ddx: acute stroke / intracranial haemorrhage / raised ICP
baseTier.action: EMERGENCY: ABCDE with AIRWAY PROTECTION (secure the airway / call for anaesthetic-airway help); correct glucose + oxygen immediately; treat the cause; urgent imaging if available; senior + critical-care help; admit. The rule holds even where intubation is limited — positioning, airway adjuncts, urgent referral.

tier.label: GCS <=8 — airway at risk
tier.action: EMERGENCY: protect the airway; correct glucose + oxygen; treat the cause; senior + critical-care help.

citation: RCP NEWS2 (ACVPU); Glasgow Coma Scale (Teasdale); WHO/UCG (cerebral malaria, meningitis). 'GCS <=8 → protect the airway.'

baseTier.label: Reduced conscious level / new confusion (GCS <=14)
baseTier.action: ABCDE; CHECK GLUCOSE IMMEDIATELY ('Don't Ever Forget Glucose'); check SpO2; review medications / toxins; focused neuro exam; treat reversible causes; serial GCS (the trend matters).

tier.label: Acute brain emergency
ddx: acute stroke / intracranial haemorrhage / raised ICP
tier.action: EMERGENCY: ABCDE; correct glucose + oxygen; treat the cause (anticonvulsant; antibiotics +/- antimalarial for CNS infection); urgent imaging if available; senior + critical-care help; admit.

citation: RCP NEWS2 (ACVPU); WHO/UCG (cerebral malaria, meningitis). Check glucose + a malaria test in EVERY reduced-consciousness patient.
